description: CRISPRi gene and pathway effects in MH and fetal bovine serum.
Content
{{n_stouffer}} significant direct FBS-versus-MH gene records (raw p < {{p_stouffer}} and |medLFC| ≥ {{lfc_cut}}), with absolute MH/FBS effects for context.
{{n_mageck}} genes with directional MAGeCK FDR < {{mageck_fdr}} in the direct B3 comparison. Significance in both directions is labelled ambiguous_bidirectional.
{{n_absolute}} gene records with separate MH and FBS effects, sensitivity/EK50 estimates and evaluation statuses.
{{n_pathways}} KEGG pathways with MH/FBS fitness summaries and GSEA statistics. Fig. 2H displays the selected pathways with sufficient paired representation.
Raw p_stouffer < {{p_stouffer}} and |medLFC| ≥ {{lfc_cut}}. Negative direct effects indicate greater depletion in FBS.
Directional MAGeCK RRA FDR < {{mageck_fdr}}, with no gene-LFC threshold.

MH and FBS profiles were estimated separately relative to the shared T0, using the same vulnerability master as Table S5. Sensitivity is a sustained binned log₂FC ≤ −1 crossing. EK50 is the fitted relative efficacy at half the effect at efficacy 1 relative to zero.

Paired, KEGG-annotated gene symbols were ranked by FBS-minus-MH medLFC and tested against sets of {{gsea_min}}–{{gsea_max}} represented genes using fgsea with {{gsea_nperm}} permutations. NES normalizes ES against permutation-derived null scores, and pathway p-values were adjusted by the Benjamini–Hochberg method.
